testInfo.title: English Level Test (CEFR)
testInfo.description: 20-question adaptive test covering vocabulary, grammar, and reading comprehension to estimate your CEFR level (A1-C2). Each question is randomly selected from a pool of 10 variants.
testInfo.source: Questions based on CEFR level descriptors and standard English proficiency testing frameworks (Cambridge, Oxford, EF SET). Vocabulary aligned with Oxford 5000 and English Vocabulary Profile.

questions.question: What is the opposite of "big"?
She ___ a student.
Which word means "a place where you can buy medicine"?
I ___ to the cinema last night.
Read: "The shop closes at 6 PM on weekdays and 4 PM on Saturdays." When does the shop close on Saturday?
Choose the correct meaning of "reliable":
options: can be trusted or depended on

questions.question: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ stay at home.
She has been working here ___ 2015.
Read: "Although the restaurant was crowded, the service was surprisingly quick and the food was excellent." What is the main idea?
options: Despite being busy, the experience was good

questions.question: The word "ambiguous" means:
options: open to more than one interpretation

questions.question: I wish I ___ more time to finish the project.
The report ___ by the time the manager arrived.
Read: "The proliferation of smartphones has fundamentally altered how people consume news, with many preferring brief updates over in-depth articles." What does this passage suggest?
options: Smartphones have changed news reading habits toward shorter content
In-depth articles are more popular than ever
Smartphones are too expensive for most people

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes: "The politician's speech was deliberately ___, avoiding any concrete commitments."
Not until the results were published ___ the extent of the problem.

Read: "The notion that creativity is an innate gift rather than a skill that can be cultivated is a pervasive misconception that discourages many from pursuing artistic endeavors." The author believes that:
options: only talented people should pursue art
creativity can be developed, contrary to popular belief

questions.question: "Ubiquitous" most closely means:
"The CEO's decision was met with opprobrium from shareholders." What does "opprobrium" mean?
Choose the correct sentence:
options: Were it not for his intervention, the project would have failed.
Was it not for his intervention, the project would have failed.
If it were not his intervention, the project would have failed.
Were not it for his intervention, the project would have failed.

questions.question: Read: "The ostensible rationale for the policy shift—fiscal prudence—belied the administration's underlying motivation to consolidate executive authority under the guise of austerity measures." The passage implies that:
options: The policy was genuinely about saving money
The stated reason for the policy was not the real reason
The administration was transparent about its goals

A1.name: Beginner
A1.description: You can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases. You can introduce yourself and ask simple questions about personal details.

A2.name: Elementary
A2.description: You can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance (e.g., personal information, shopping, local geography).

B1.name: Intermediate
B1.description: You can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters. You can deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling.

B2.name: Upper Intermediate
B2.description: You can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics. You can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity.

C1.name: Advanced
C1.description: You can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts and recognize implicit meaning. You can express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions.

C2.name: Mastery
C2.description: You can understand with ease virtually everything heard or read. You can summarize information from different sources, reconstructing arguments in a coherent presentation.
